details: 24 Oct, owner asked how to record the front's effort in relay. profiles/active.toml has [session] model = "opus", effort = "high" and calls itself "the setup every session runs", but only lib/relay_bench.py reads [session]; relay sync never writes them, and ~/.claude/settings.json holds effortLevel "high" set by hand. A change to [session] (an adopted candidate, say) silently does nothing for real sessions.
failing_case: Set [session] effort = "medium" in profiles/active.toml and run `relay sync`: ~/.claude/settings.json still says effortLevel "high".
pass_cases: After `relay sync` the settings carry the profile's model and effortLevel, other keys untouched; `relay sync --dry` names the change; a second sync is unchanged.
reason: tests/test_session_profile.py:45 test_sync_writes_model_and_effort_and_leaves_other_keys passes at head, fails at 76c37c3.

details: CONFIRMED by reading Claude Code 2.1.310 (the installed binary). b2t(): for userSettings the top-level effortLevel
goes to `legacyUserEffort` (setsTopLevel false); per-model values come from modelSettings. U2r(table, model):
byModel[model] wins; otherwise, with no default from another source, legacyUserEffort applies only when
Y2o(model) holds, which is true for the listed older models (claude-opus-4-x, claude-opus-5, sonnet-4-x, ...)
or names that do not parse; claude-opus-5-5 parses and is not on the list, so the top-level user effortLevel is
ignored for it entirely. And the real file already holds modelSettings.claude-opus-5-5.effortLevel "high", which
wins in any case. The fixer saw the modelSettings copy (report: "not touched") but did not check which one is read.
The tests encode only the top-level shape, so they pass while the real session is unchanged.
The key is canonical (TV(name)); the profile holds the alias "opus", so the fix must know the id the alias
resolves to, or the profile must name the id. That may need the owner's word (see the question in fix_hint).
evidence: Tool doc in binary: "takes effortLevel only and saves it as the default for the session's current model, under modelSettings as /effort saves it"
failing_case: Real shape today: ~/.claude/settings.json has model "opus" and modelSettings {"claude-opus-5-5": {"effortLevel": "high"}},
no top-level effortLevel (this is where /effort saves it). Set [session] effort = "medium" and run relay sync:
it writes top-level effortLevel "medium", doctor prints ok, and a new Opus 5.5 session still runs at high.
Should: the session for the profile's model runs at medium.
fix_hint: Write modelSettings[<canonical id of the profile's model>].effortLevel (keep or drop top-level effortLevel), and make
doctor compare that entry. The canonical id: either resolve the alias the way the front's model resolves today
(e.g. the key already present in modelSettings whose family matches the alias), or have [session] model name the
full id. Add a test with the real shape (pass case 1).
pass_cases: after sync the effort Claude Code resolves for claude-opus-5-5 is medium (modelSettings entry for that model is "medium").
2. same file, other keys (theme, enabledPlugins, modelSettings.<other model>.autoCompactWindow) untouched.
3. sync --dry names the change and writes nothing; a second sync says unchanged.
4. doctor reports FIX when modelSettings.<profile model>.effortLevel differs from [session] effort, even if top-level effortLevel matches.
5. settings with no modelSettings at all: after sync the profile's effort applies to the profile's model.
reason: tests/test_session_profile.py:77,86,92,99 pass; fail at 2f7988f (three of four; the no-modelsettings case passed before by design).
findings.summary: the top-level effortLevel sync writes is ignored by Claude Code for the front's model; modelSettings.<model>.effortLevel wins, so the item's failing case still holds and doctor says ok

details: CONFIRMED: reproduced in a temp CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, sync wrote "effortLevel": "max". Claude Code 2.1.310 schema:
effortLevel:B(["low","medium","high","xhigh"]).optional().catch(void 0); its tool doc says "'max' is session-only and
is not written". The docstring of session_settings names the four values but nothing enforces them. Size: 10.
failing_case: Profile [session] effort = "max" (the tune skill and docs/benchmark.md list max as an effort; `relay candidate --set
session.effort=max` then adopt). relay sync writes effortLevel "max": state "set effortLevel None -> 'max'".
Claude Code's schema for the persisted effort is low|medium|high|xhigh with .catch(undefined), so the value is
dropped silently and the session runs at the model default; doctor says ok. Should: sync and doctor say plainly
that max cannot be persisted (or refuse it), and write nothing invalid.
fix_hint: A fixed tuple of persistable values beside SESSION_KEYS; a value outside it gives a state "not written: max is
pass_cases: 1. effort "max": sync state names that max is session-only and not written; settings.json effort keys unchanged.
2. effort "max": doctor reports FIX (or a note) rather than ok.
findings.summary: [session] effort "max" is written to settings.json, where Claude Code drops it (max is session-only), and doctor reports ok

details: CONFIRMED by reproduction. read_json maps ValueError to {} and merge_session_settings then writes. merge_user_settings
had the same flaw but ran only in setup --global/install; this change puts it on the path of every `relay sync`,
`relay improve adopt` and install. The backup makes it recoverable, but sessions lose the relay plugins and
evidence: sync -> "set effortLevel None -> 'max', model None -> 'opus'"; settings.json now {"model": "opus", "effortLevel": "max"};
failing_case: ~/.claude/settings.json is not valid JSON (a trailing comma after a hand edit):
relay sync -> read_json returns {}, the file becomes {"model": "opus", "effortLevel": "max"}; enabledPlugins,
permissions, marketplaces are gone from the live file (a .bak is kept). Should: sync refuses that target with
"settings.json is not valid JSON: <error>" and leaves the file as it is.
fix_hint: Read the file with a parser that tells "missing" from "invalid"; on invalid return (path, REFUSED + reason) / WOULD_REFUSE
in dry. Applying the same to merge_user_settings is cheap and in the same file.
pass_cases: 1. malformed settings.json: sync state starts with "refused: " (so report_refused exits 1), file byte-identical, no .bak written.
2. sync --dry on the malformed file: "would refuse: ..." and nothing written.
3. missing settings.json: sync creates it with model and effortLevel (works today).
4. valid file: merged as today, other keys untouched.
findings.summary: every relay sync now rewrites a malformed settings.json as just model and effortLevel, dropping plugins, permissions and hooks
